notes:
Lead profile: SMB e‑commerce chat plugin company. Mostly public cloud, self-serve signups.

Key pain: unpredictable 429s during traffic spikes (promo emails, flash sales). Engineer note: "We get 429s for ~60s bursts then OK — users see failed messages and retry loop." Wants simple client guidance and a short-term way to allow bursts.

Requirements summary:
- Workload: live support/chat with occasional bulk rerank jobs for triage. Real-time constraints for chat (p95 target ~250ms response for short queries).
- Throughput: typical steady state 20-50 qps, peak bursts up to ~400 qps for 30–90s windows during promos.
- Cost sensitivity: high — trying to keep monthly infra under $2k while preserving UX.
- Model preference: small/medium open model variants for cost; willing to try quantized options.
- Routing/fallback: needs automatic fallback to a cheaper/shorter-context variant when concurrency hits soft limits.
- Security: SOC2 important for resellers; SSO for internal ops portal.

Current engineering concerns:
- How hosted API enforces quotas vs. transient concurrency limits? want guarantees about short burst allowances (burst tokens, leaky-bucket behavior).
- Best-practice retry/backoff settings to avoid thundering herd.
- Clear guidance on how to request temporary quota uplift during marketing campaigns.

Sales notes/asks:
- Provide a short one-pager that explains: rate limit semantics, 429 meaning in our system, recommended client retry (exponential backoff + capped jitter), and example code snippets.
- Offer a one-time trial burst uplift (7 days) to validate UX; must include observable metrics dashboard during test.

Quoted from call: "If our users see the bot fail during checkout, it's a showstopper. We need a predictable short-burst policy or a hands-on uplift path."
